# OpenUtau historical-serializer USTX fixtures

These six files were generated by `tools/openutau_oracle/Program.cs`
(`--emit-fixture`, `--emit-curve-fixture`, or `--emit-multiline-fixture`)
built separately against the named OpenUtau source tags.
They are **serializer-generated**, not hand-edited copies of a 0.9 file and
not claims of a human operating the historical desktop GUI. The tool creates
one `UProject` with two tempo events, two meters, a stereo-positioned track,
two Japanese-lyric notes, pitch points and vibrato; it validates the project,
calls OpenUtau `BeforeSave`, and writes the exact YAML from that version's
`Yaml.DefaultSerializer` with `Encoding.UTF8`, including its BOM. Nonzero
per-note `tuning` is set only when that version's `UNote` model has the field.

Generation used .NET SDK 10.0.401. Each historical checkout's
`OpenUtau.Core.csproj` needed a **build-only resource-name metadata patch**:
distinct `LogicalName` and `ManifestResourceName` values on its multiple
`Resources.resx` items. Otherwise that SDK reports MSB3577 because those
resources resolve to the same intermediate filename. No serializer/model
source was edited. The temporary checkouts retain their exact Git HEADs;
this repository retains the resulting fixture bytes and hashes. The 0.6
build also emitted NETSDK1206 for old platform-specific ONNX Runtime assets.
Those old packages are used here only to generate inert score YAML and are
not shipped with SEAM.

The curve file exercises a nonempty `dyn` expression curve with 64 x/y pairs.
It is 6,584 bytes and 437 lines, versus 306 lines for the empty-curve 0.9
file. The 131-line increase includes 128 point lines. SEAM now maps its
standard `dyn` curve into bounded dynamics automation and exports it again;
the pinned OpenUtau sampler measured zero difference at 289 five-tick grid
positions. This is not a claim about arbitrary curve types or audio. The
default parser caps input at 4 MiB,
100,000 physical lines/nodes and 50,000 entries per sequence. Therefore a
large real-world curve can fail closed before import even when the musical
notes fit. The regression exercises a 400-node and 50-entry reduced budget;
it does not establish a universal safe maximum for user-authored projects.

Each file passed its own version's `Ustx.Load` and pinned OpenUtau `8c0dc40`'s
`Ustx.Load`. SEAM's native importer accepted the original four and disclosed 9, 9,
10 and 10 conversion issues respectively (the extra 0.8/0.9 issue says that
the separate tuning edit control is flattened into pitch automation). SEAM
re-exported all four as 0.9; pinned OpenUtau loaded each result. The oracle's
`--compare-pitch` uses OpenUtau's pitch sampler on 18 fixed in-note points per
pair: maximum error was 0.160040, 0.160040, 0.160039 and 0.160039 cents.
As a negative control, changing only the first note's round-tripped tuning to
10 cents made the same comparison fail (10.105982 cents maximum error, exit 1).
This excludes vibrato modulation and does not prove every possible curve,
actual rendered sound, or historical GUI operation.

The curve file also passed its historical and pinned loaders, SEAM
import/export and pinned-loader reimport. Before the dynamics increment, its
curve loss brought the SEAM import report to 11 issues; the current import
reports 10, with no loss for the supported curve. Authored pitch remained
within 0.160039 cents on the same 18-point grid in the earlier comparison.
The sixth file retains the former failing probe: the
historical serializer emitted a folded `>-` project comment whose content
includes `#`, `&`, `*`, and `!`. SEAM now imports it without interpreting those
characters as YAML operators; its original historical loader, pinned loader,
SEAM import/export, pinned re-load and pitch sampler pass (0.160039 cents
maximum on the same grid). Block-scalar tests also exercise literal/folded
lyric values, chomping, explicit indentation and resource limits. The
nonempty project comment is explicitly reported as a loss (11 import issues,
not silently discarded). This is
controlled serializer evidence, not every possible user-authored YAML shape.
